newsitem.title: FRANCE: AOM denies report on Air Liberte takeover plan.
newsitem.headline: AOM denies report on Air Liberte takeover plan.

text.p: The chairman of French private airline AOM denied on Friday a French newspaper report that the company was part of a plan to buy the insolvent Air Liberte airline to form a new group to block British Airways Plc.
An AOM spokeswoman told Reuters, "Mr (Alexandre) Couvelaire has formally denied the information in Le Monde published this afternoon."

In London, British Airways said it had urged the European Transport and Competition Commissioners to block a bid by AOM for Air Liberte. Le Monde reported the state wanted AOM and Euralaire to buy Air Liberte to create a new French group.
The AOM spokeswoman did not deny AOM was interested in Air Liberte. She gave no further details.

The newspaper reported AOM chairman Alexandre Couvelaire would buy 51 percent of AOM, along with other investors, from CDR, to allow the airline to bid for Air Liberte. That is necessary as CDR was set up to sell assets, not buy them.
AOM is owned by the Consortium de Realisation (CDR), the holding company charged with selling Credit Lyonnais assets under a state-backed rescue plan.
The AOM and Air Liberte merged company would then buy privately-owned Euralair, the report said.

BA said allowing AOM to buy Air Liberte would mean adding to CDR's liabilities in contravention to the conditions for aid for Credit Lyonnais. It said it had been told by offical sources that AOM, or its representatives, was on the point of making an offer for Air Liberte.
Air Liberte was placed under legal administration insolvency on September 26.
It made a loss of 160 million francs in the first six months of 1996 although it had forecast profit of 20 million francs, Couvelaire said on August 29.
BA earlier said its French TAT European Airlines subsidiary was in touch with the administrators to assess Air Liberte's assets.
